verdict.rationale: OpenTofu's first-party docs state it encrypts state and plan files at rest, for both local storage and backends, and also with the terraform_remote_state data source (opentofu-docs-9, opentofu-docs-20). An AES-GCM encryption method is documented (opentofu-docs-19), and community commentary welcomes state encryption as a shipped feature (opentofu-comm-10). The community question about committing encrypted state to a public repo is general skepticism, not a contradiction. Missing for 10: detail on key-provider and key-management options, key rotation or migration of existing plaintext state, and independent hands-on verification that encrypted files are unreadable.
